关键词: Mexico Training and Employment Program, Phase II
主要内容: On July 25, 2013, the U.S. Department of the Treasury recognized exceptional development projects and initiatives undertaken by the Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) at the second annual Development Impact Honors ceremony. The event, held in Washington, brought together leaders from MDBs, Members of Congress, development and business community leaders, and senior administration officials to celebrate excellence in development. The projects honored reflect efforts to strengthen communities and advance American economic and security interests globally. Secretary Jacob J. Lew highlighted the importance of these projects, emphasizing their role in promoting clean energy, women’s economic equality, food security, and support for vulnerable populations. The projects were evaluated based on effectiveness, quality of work, and success in overcoming development challenges. Notable projects included the Cote d’Ivoire Project, which addressed gender-based violence through integrated services and community engagement, and the Uganda Community Agricultural Infrastructure Program, which improved rural infrastructure and economic opportunities. The Bhutan Green Power Project, supported by the Asian Development Bank, exemplifies sustainable development initiatives that align with U.S. priorities. The U.S. Department of the Treasury recognized multilateral development banks (MDBs) at its annual awards ceremony, highlighting their critical role in promoting economic growth, rural development, and environmental protection. One notable project was Bhutan’s collaboration with the private sector to create a run-of-the-river hydropower facility, which replaced fossil fuel-generated power with clean energy sources. The project extended hydroelectricity grids to over 8,700 rural households and facilities and introduced solar power systems to electrify schools, health clinics, and community centers in remote areas. Another initiative was the Mexico Training and Employment Program, Phase II, led by the Inter-American Development Bank. This program addressed the gap between training programs and employer needs by involving private employers in on-the-job training. From 2010 to 2012, it provided stipends to hundreds of thousands of people, helped secure employment for 1.5 million, and created a platform for job and training searches. The project also focused on vulnerable groups, including women, youth, and disabled workers. The Post-Earthquake Assessment Project in Haiti, led by the World Bank Group, showcased the role of MDBs in disaster response. The 2010 earthquake caused massive destruction, and the project aimed to restore basic services by assessing buildings, collecting damage data, and strengthening national institutions. Over 400,000 buildings were evaluated at a cost of $10 per building, facilitating safe reoccupation and recovery.
